+# R74 literature and mathematical priority addendum
+
+This addendum covers the active R74 mathematics. The full R73 literature ledger remains an inherited record. The comparisons below use primary papers, author preprints, and publisher records; each source summary is below 200 words. They delimit the claims actually proved here. They are not an exhaustive novelty clearance, an independent specialist assessment, or an editorial decision.
+
+## 1. Historical priority inside this manuscript
+
+The full historical audit identified a substantive duplication during development: the initially proposed R74 uniform-posterior instrument theorem, physical-state dictionary, algebraic construction, and dictionary noise exponent were already proved in `sections/27-interior-instruments.tex` in R68 and retained in R73. The active R74 text therefore refers to the existing authorities rather than renumbering those results as a new contribution.
+
+The retained R68 results are stronger than those development drafts. `thm:r68-instrument` permits multiple preparation anchors, sparse branch rows, full stopped laws including nontermination, and nonnegative mean cost observables. `cor:r68-risk` gives same-policy risk/resource transfer for the declared unknown-family setting. `prop:r68-algebraic` supplies exact algebraic synthesis and margin search. `thm:r68-block` counts the clock for several-step interiority. `thm:r68-noise-exponent` proves the stronger universal lower bound `s^(-(d-1))` and finite-command state-positive witnesses. The duplicate drafts are preserved under `provenance/author-research/superseded`; they are excluded from the R74 mathematical increment.
+
+Similarly, the sharp four-period count at `1/sqrt(3)` already follows from `thm:r69-sector-phase` and `prop:r73-period-four`. R74 records that closure accurately. Its finite-probe certificate remains a different inherited result. Existing R73 normal forms, decoder obstruction, algebraic synthesis, and periodic-memory results are not renamed R74 discoveries.
+
+## 2. Symmetry, positive factorizations, and terminal contrast
+
+### GPT13 — symmetric cone lifts are established theory
+
+J. Gouveia, P. A. Parrilo and R. R. Thomas, *Lifts of convex sets and cone factorizations*, Mathematics of Operations Research **38**(2) (2013), 248–264. DOI: [10.1287/moor.1120.0575](https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.1120.0575). [Primary author text](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.3164).
+
+The full primary preprint was opened; Theorems 2.4 and 2.12 were inspected. They connect cone lifts with factorizations of slack operators and treat equivariance. R74 therefore does not claim to introduce symmetric positive factorizations. Its assertions concern the particular all-word stochastic realization invariant inherited from R73: a common finite group action, probability-valued preparation and decoder, the exact minimum permutation-module value at small terminal contrast, and the prescribed-start charge. A finite response table is not automatically the complete slack operator of its residual body; that identification is not silently assumed.
+
+### KPT10 — the full journal article is from 2012
+
+V. Kaibel, K. Pashkovich and D. O. Theis, *Symmetry matters for sizes of extended formulations*, SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics **26**(3) (2012), 1361–1382. DOI: [10.1137/110839813](https://doi.org/10.1137/110839813). [Primary author text](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0911.3712).
+
+The key `KPT10` is retained as an identifier, not a publication-year assertion. The preliminary IPCO version appeared in 2010, LNCS 6080, 135–148. The [publisher record](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/110839813) confirms the full article's 2012 volume and pages. Definition 11 and Lemma 12 discuss coordinate-symmetric sections. Symmetry constraints can change positive-lift complexity; that broad phenomenon is established. The specific R74 step is that normal orbit stabilizers allow preparation to be absorbed into a bounded quotient decoder without increasing the counted core. This yields the exact subgroup-family LP, rather than a generic claim that all symmetric factorizations are linear programs.
+
+### GillisGlineur12 — restricted and unrestricted positive factorizations differ
+
+N. Gillis and F. Glineur, *On the geometric interpretation of the nonnegative rank*, Linear Algebra and its Applications **437**(11) (2012), 2685–2712. DOI: [10.1016/j.laa.2012.06.038](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.laa.2012.06.038). [Primary author text](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1009.0880).
+
+The primary preprint and its restricted-rank formulation were inspected. A factorization whose hidden columns are confined to the target column space imposes an additional restriction; general positive realizations cannot be identified with that geometry without proof. R74 retains the R73 common-action normal form and does not project every hidden response into the reached observable plane. The contrast construction embeds the observable module into a permutation module and builds legal probabilities there. The quotient LP is justified by a separate normality argument. The DOI ends in **038**; an erroneous **031** suffix encountered in a development bibliography was corrected.
+
+### BocciCarliniRapallo11 — mixing and perturbation persistence are not new principles
+
+C. Bocci, E. Carlini and F. Rapallo, *Perturbation of matrices and nonnegative rank with a view toward statistical models*, SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications **32**(4) (2011), 1500–1512. DOI: [10.1137/110825455](https://doi.org/10.1137/110825455). [Primary author text](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1010.3566).
+
+Theorem 3.1 and Proposition 3.2 were inspected; the [publisher record](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/110825455) was checked. The paper treats local nondecrease and barycentric perturbations of ordinary nonnegative rank. R74 makes no general first claim for positivity under mixing or persistence of a rank obstruction. Its additional conclusions are the exact group permutation-module saturation value, attained action-budget endpoints, and explicit quotient payoff certificates. The C2^4 perturbation radius is a sufficient quantitative certificate for tables on the same command quotient; it is not asserted sharp, nor does it give a matching upper for all nearby tables.
+
+## 3. Realization theory, conditional dynamics, and the active R74 increment
+
+### Heller65 — inherited positive-realization authority
+
+A. Heller, *On stochastic processes derived from Markov chains*, Annals of Mathematical Statistics **36**(4) (1965), 1286–1291. DOI: [10.1214/aoms/1177700000](https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177700000). [Primary publisher record](https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-mathematical-statistics/volume-36/issue-4/On-Stochastic-Processes-Derived-From-Markov-Chains/10.1214/aoms/1177700000.full).
+
+This classical authority is retained from the earlier manuscript's positive-realization ledger. The publisher metadata were verified in this pass; the attempted full primary PDF returned a security check and was not treated as a full-text read. No new theorem-number comparison with Heller is claimed. The active R74 proofs explicitly construct their invariant polytopes and stochastic rows, so no missing construction is delegated to an inaccessible citation.
+
+### MonrasWinter14 — quantum realization and cone methods are prior work
+
+A. Monras and A. Winter, *Quantum learning of classical stochastic processes: The completely-positive realization problem*, TQC 2014, LIPIcs **27** (2014), 99–109. DOI: [10.4230/LIPIcs.TQC.2014.99](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.TQC.2014.99). [Primary proceedings and PDF](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.TQC.2014.99).
+
+The primary proceedings PDF was opened and its realization discussion inspected. It treats quantum instruments, linear quasi-realizations, positive cones and completely positive realization. Thus invariant-cone and quantum hidden-state mechanisms precede R74. The common-contraction result is presented as a quantified constructive consequence: a supplied norm and legal decoder ball produce one polytope for all mixed command words, with an explicit prefix/core label bound. It asserts neither a new abstract positive-realization criterion nor a decision procedure for joint spectral radius. Its contrast with earlier special unary background constructions is a scope extension, not a claim to originate the mechanism.
+
+### Okay26 — adaptive polyhedral instrument simulation is explicit prior art
+
+C. Okay, *Polyhedral classical simulators for quantum computation*, Research in the Mathematical Sciences **13** (2026), article 55. DOI: [10.1007/s40687-026-00626-x](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40687-026-00626-x). [Open primary full text](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40687-026-00626-x).
+
+The full publisher text, Theorem 16, Lemma 17 and Corollary 19 were inspected. They supply updates from a preserved simulation polytope, prove adaptive composition, and recover the output distribution. R74 must credit this mechanism. In this manuscript the quantitative posterior-floor construction was already established in R68 and remains inherited. The active new conditional-memory family uses explicit normalized branch geometry for its upper and a separate relative-spectral argument for its lower. The latter is a response-level exact count; it is not a first claim of polyhedral adaptive simulation. The source's publication date is 2 June 2026 and was checked against the current publisher record.
+
+### Fanizza24 — peripheral-phase obstructions and phase-dependent memory are prior mechanisms
+
+M. Fanizza, J. Lumbreras and A. Winter, *Quantum theory in finite dimension cannot explain every general process with finite memory*, Communications in Mathematical Physics **405** (2024), article 50. DOI: [10.1007/s00220-023-04913-4](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00220-023-04913-4). [Primary publisher full text](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00220-023-04913-4); [author preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.11225).
+
+Section 2.3 was inspected in the full publisher text. It explicitly recalls the FRDN noncommensurate-phase Perron–Frobenius obstruction and discusses minimal classical dimension for commensurate phases, citing Dharmadhikari–Nadkarni (1970). Therefore neither the phase-order/infinite-memory dichotomy nor its peripheral-spectrum mechanism is claimed first in R74. The current family combines a fixed qubit, rank three, three uniformly positive outcomes, an exactly depolarizing average channel and one-dependence, and proves a separate sharp counted-pure-start increment from `q` to `q+1`. The earlier primary 1970 article is identified through that discussion; its full proof was not independently reread in this pass. No worldwide novelty clearance is inferred from this comparison.
+
+### HolroydLiggett16 — one-dependent processes need not be finite hidden Markov
+
+A. E. Holroyd and T. M. Liggett, *Finitely dependent coloring*, Forum of Mathematics, Pi **4** (2016), e9. DOI: [10.1017/fmp.2016.7](https://doi.org/10.1017/fmp.2016.7). [Primary author PDF](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/4col.pdf).
+
+The introduction, Theorem 1, Proposition 3 and Section 5 were inspected. The paper gives a stationary one-dependent coloring and proves the hidden-Markov obstruction attributed there to Schramm. +### AubrunSzarek17 — convex approximation of density matrices is established and stronger in dimension
+
+G. Aubrun and S. J. Szarek, *Dvoretzky's theorem and the complexity of entanglement detection*, Discrete Analysis (2017), paper 1, 20 pp. DOI: [10.19086/da.1242](https://doi.org/10.19086/da.1242). [Primary author text](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1510.00578).

+Section 6 and Proposition 10 were inspected. The latter gives pure-state convex approximations with exponential dependence on dimension for a fixed shrinkage. R68's elementary net bound is therefore not presented as the best available dimension dependence. Its declared small-noise exponent concerns one physical dictionary covering every state in the shrunken density body, and the R68 proof remains current. +H. Fawzi, *On polyhedral approximations of the positive semidefinite cone*, Mathematics of Operations Research **46**(4) (2021), 1479–1489. +## The current theorem center
+
+The inherited reversible classification and stochastic normal form establish the starting point. For a finite-dimensional compactly reversible response, exact finite stochastic realizability is equivalent to finiteness of the observable group. Every finite realization reduces, without increasing its live-label count, to a permutation core and at most one counted initializer. For a finite observable group `G`, residual count `N`, and least positive permutation-factorization size `kappa_G(b)`,
+
+\[
+ m(b)=\min\{N,1+\kappa_G(b)\}.
+\]
+
+This is a complete inherited theorem, not a conjectural assumption of R74. The preparation and decoder in the factorization must be nonnegative and normalized. The dimension of a containing permutation module is a lower bound; it need not be the optimum at full contrast. R74 studies and partly resolves that positivity problem, then compares it with the resource carried by observed instrument branches.
+
+### 1. Universal finite-group attainment at small terminal contrast
+
+Let `pi` be the group average of a nonconstant response and `b_t=pi+t(b-pi)`, `0<=t<=1`. `thm:r74-low-contrast` proves, for every finite observable group and every finite outcome alphabet, that some explicit `t_0>0` satisfies
+
+\[
+ \kappa_G(b_t)=\nu_G(V_b),\qquad
+ m(b_t)=\min\{N,1+\nu_G(V_b)\}\quad(0<t\le t_0).
+\]
+
+Here `nu_G(V_b)` is the least cardinality of a permutation action whose real module contains the observable response module. The proof embeds the zero-average part, perturbs the uniform preparation within the probability simplex, and scales a zero-row-sum decoder perturbation. Its explicit constants ensure positivity. Outputs with zero group average are identically zero and are harmless. Positive contrast preserves the group, module and residual equality pattern; zero contrast is a separate one-label degeneracy.
+
+This is a theorem for arbitrary finite groups, not a statement restricted to an abelian, fixed-rank, binary, or qubit model. It does not say that small positive contrast makes an infinite compact observable group finitely realizable: the unchanged infinite group still obstructs every finite exact realization. For prepared unitary commands the contrast is realized by mixing the terminal POVM with the constant group-average readout, without changing the commands.
+
+`thm:r74-contrast-thresholds` further proves that, for each core budget `k`, the set of feasible contrasts is a closed initial interval `[0,tau_k]`. Its endpoint is attained and lower memory is retained at that endpoint. The thresholds are nondecreasing, `tau_N=1`, budgets below the module minimum have endpoint zero, and the module-minimum budget has a positive endpoint. Algebraic input makes the thresholds computable real algebraic numbers. This does not give a universal elementary closed formula or a polynomial algorithm.
+
+### 2. Exact quotient optimization and payoff duality
+
+If every subgroup of `G` is normal, `lem:r74-normal-orbits` absorbs the mixed preparation inside each quotient orbit into its decoder. Repeated copies of the same quotient can be merged. This reduces positive factorization to a finite selection of distinct subgroups `H` with cost `sum_H [G:H]` and nonnegative quotient tables `f_H` of constant row mass `p_H`, satisfying
+
+\[
+ \sum_c f_H(q,c)=p_H,\qquad
+ \sum_Hp_H=1,\qquad
+ \sum_Hf_H(Hg,c)=b(g,c).
+\]
+
+`thm:r74-quotient-lp` proves that the least feasible cost is exactly `kappa_G(b)`. The minimal observable residual count in this class is `|G|`; hence the pure-start minimum is `min{|G|,1+kappa_G(b)}`. Rational data admit rational optimal tables. Data in a specified real algebraic number field admit a controller in that same field. These conclusions include every finite abelian group and also the finite nonabelian groups whose subgroups are all normal. Normality is used in the absorption proof and is not omitted.
+
+For a selected family, `thm:r74-quotient-dual` computes its support function as the maximum, over its quotients, of a sum of cosetwise best-output payoffs. All signed-payoff inequalities are necessary and sufficient for feasibility. Infeasibility has a strict rational witness, and its margin yields a quantitative table-perturbation exclusion. Contrast endpoints have attained primal and dual LP descriptions, including degenerate affine-hull cases. The budget optimum still requires a finite combinatorial family selection: one family witness does not automatically separate the entire union of all low-cost families.
+
+For abelian groups, `cor:r74-abelian-cover` computes the module minimum from character support and quotient-character covers. It is exact for sufficiently small contrast. At larger contrast, the actual table can force additional positive states even while that support is unchanged.
+
+### 3. Matching model laws and a robust finite-table lower
+
+The new exact examples expose the distinction between representation data and positivity.
+
+| Response family | Fixed positive-parameter data | Exact core / pure-start memory |
+|---|---|---|
+| Prepared-qubit `S_3` response `beta_t(g)=1/2+(t/4)uP_gu^T`, `u=(1,-1,0)` | Observable group `S_3`, dimension three, six residuals | Core three and pure-start four for `0<t<=2/3`; core and pure-start six for `2/3<t<=1`; one at zero. |
+| Five-character circuit on `(F_2)^4`, `beta_t=3/8+(t/8)sum_{i=1}^5 chi_i` | Dimension six, sixteen residuals, permutation-module minimum ten | Core ten / pure-start eleven for `0<t<=3/5`; core twelve / pure-start thirteen above `3/5`; one at zero. |
+
+The `S_3` lower examines every action of size at most five. An explicit four-matrix spanning argument forces the standard-component preparation and decoder to have the stated rank-one directions; their separate probability bounds give `t<=2/3`. The upper realizes every group response, including the endpoint.
+
+The four-bit lower classifies every possible quotient family of cost at most eleven. Its active character blocks must partition a five-element circuit into singletons and pairs. A signed payoff for each partition has nonnegative averages on the relevant quotient fibers and target value `(3-5t)/8`. This excludes all those families above `3/5`. A degree-ten construction attains the low branch; a four-point plus eight-point construction attains the high branch by exact Fourier cancellation.
+
+`cor:r74-circuit-robust` extends the lower to any binary probability table on the same group and generator quotient within supremum distance `(5t-3)/18` of the target, for `t>3/5`. All five active coefficients survive, and every candidate partition has a witness of normalized absolute sum at most `9/4`. Consequently its core needs at least twelve labels and its pure-start memory at least thirteen. This is a sufficient lower neighborhood, not a sharp radius or a matching thirteen-label upper for every perturbed table. The sixteen-dimensional diagonal physical implementation of this example is classical; no quantum advantage is claimed for it.
+
+### 4. A common contracting probability-response realization
+
+`thm:r74-contraction` treats a supplied linear response `b(w,c)=p_c+ell_c(x_w)` with `x_{wa}=F_a x_w`. Assume one norm contracts every command by `rho<1`, the actual response is probabilistically valid, and a radius `r` satisfies `r||ell_c||_*<=p_c` for every output. A finite net supplies a polytope containing `rho` times the unit ball and contained in the unit ball, invariant under all command maps after scaling. Transient prefix labels lead into this common recurrent polytope. With `a` commands and `rho^(T-1)||x_0||<=r`, the count is at most
+
+\[
+ \sum_{j=0}^{T-1}a^j+
+ \left\lceil\left(1+\frac{2}{1-\rho}\right)^n\right\rceil.
+\]
+
+All decoder rows are bounded probabilities; the empty-word label and first transition are counted. This is a sufficient construction, without minimality or efficiency claims. It uses classical invariant-polytope realization and should be assessed as a quantitative corollary with these operational conventions. A supplied uniform product-decay certificate yields a suitable common norm; the theorem does not decide joint spectral radius.
+
+This differs from the retained unique-decision convergence theorem: a discontinuous sign selector can keep changing despite physical contraction. It also does not contradict the retained leakage obstruction with a vanishing limiting output, because that example fails the whole-ball decoder margin.
+
+### 5. A sharp conditional-memory law in a fixed qubit
+
+`thm:r74-depolarizing-obstruction` uses three completely positive branches on a qubit. Their sum is exactly the completely depolarizing channel, and their probabilities are respectively `1/8`, a value in `[1/16,3/16]`, and a value in `[11/16,13/16]`, for every incoming state. From `I/2` the outcome process is stationary and one-dependent. Its word-Hankel rank is exactly three.
+
+If the conditional phase has order `q>=3`, the minimum classical hidden-state count is exactly `q` with a free mixed initialization and `q+1` with a pure counted initialization. A regular `q`-gon gives one positive realization for all branches. The strict third-branch bound `5/11<1/2` keeps its normalized output inside that polygon. A stationary hidden initial distribution also exists without enlarging the count.
+
+For the lower, the cylinder `1 0^n 1` carries three distinct exponential modes. Every classical realization has an active nonnegative zero-branch block whose relative peripheral spectrum contains the phase. Irreducibility propagates the phase relation to every positive edge, so every cycle length is a multiple of `q`. At exactly `q` states the block is a weighted full cycle. A pure starting point and the probabilities of `0^n` force all weights to be `1/8`; the probabilities of `0^n1` force constant terminal masses, contradicting the oscillating cylinder already at `11`. This proves the exact initializer charge. A phase of infinite order cannot occur in any finite positive block, ruling out all finite classical realizations with arbitrary real entries.
+
+The irrational algebraic phase `(3+4i)/5` yields rational superoperator coefficients and infinite memory. This is not the first quantum process without a finite classical realization, the first one-dependent non-HMM process, or the first commensurate/irrational phase memory distinction. The manuscript credits the existing positive-realization and FRDN antecedents, including the explicit comparison in Fanizza–Lumbreras–Winter. The new assertion is the simultaneous fixed-qubit, rank-three, uniform-outcome-floor, exactly depolarizing and one-dependent family with the precise mixed/pure resource law. Its lower is unrestricted classical response memory, stronger than a lower restricted to physical-state dictionaries.

+# Theorem and dependency map — General Theta Foundations I, R74
+
+The current paired native build contains **197 indexed theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary and example labels**: all 185 predecessor labels and twelve additions. Eleven additions are in the main article and one supplement corollary explicitly records an inherited R69 result. This is an inventory, not a novelty count. The independent R58 companion has its own numbering and complete source.
+
+## Minimal proof chains and mathematical roles
+
+| Chain | Generality, proof authority and boundary |
+|---|---|
+| Predictive response → compact reversibility → finite group → stochastic normal form | Retained R72/R73 results for arbitrary finite-dimensional compactly reversible probability responses. Full recurrent-projection proof is in the current supplement. |
+| Normal form → small-contrast module saturation → attained thresholds | New R74 structure for every finite observable group and every finite terminal output set; positive contrast preserves the observable data, while zero contrast is a separate degeneracy. |
+| Normal stabilizers → quotient LP → payoff dual → optimal arithmetic realization | Necessary and sufficient unrestricted optimization when every subgroup is normal; otherwise only the stated restricted normal-stabilizer class. Classical LP/QE ingredients are credited. |
+| Representation/Fourier constraints → matching controllers and duals | Exact `S_3` and four-bit model transitions; the robust four-bit neighbourhood has a lower bound only. |
+| Retained posterior-interiority → common physical dictionary → complete adaptive/stopped laws | R68, not a new R74 claim. Several preparations, sparse rows, block clocks, algebraic synthesis and state-positive noise exponent retain their original scope. |
+| Common norm + decoder ball → invariant polytope + counted prefixes | New quantified constructive consequence of classical positive realization. It assumes a supplied common contraction certificate and asserts no optimal count. |
+| Displayed qubit branches → rank-three cylinder → relative peripheral phase → cycle rigidity | Exact mixed/pure memory `q` / `q+1` or infinity, with matching polygon realization. Prior phase mechanisms and earlier one-dependent non-HMM processes are credited. |
+| R69 first sector → period-four corollary | Inherited exact threshold, recorded to correct stale open-status wording. The R73 finite-probe certificate remains valid and nonsharp. |
+| Actual-history / performed-law / minimax / dual / reset / rank / geometric chains | Separate retained results with their own hypotheses. Their preservation does not make them all prerequisites for the new group and instrument theorems. |
+
+Detailed hypotheses, direct proof prerequisites, argument summaries, source snapshots and priority boundaries for the twelve additions are in [THEOREM_DEPENDENCIES_R74.md](THEOREM_DEPENDENCIES_R74.md) and `provenance/R74_PROOF_DEPENDENCIES.json`. The complete 197-entry current catalog is `THEOREM_DEPENDENCIES.json`; the exact predecessor ledger and original historical ledgers remain retained. Extracted syntactic references and declared proof dependencies are kept distinct.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Independent finite diagnostic of the proposed five-character obstruction.
+
+This exhausts quotient-action families in the finite four-bit group. It does
+not establish the general finite-group structural theorem or novelty.
+"""
+import collections
+import itertools
+import json
+from fractions import Fraction as Q
+
+checks=0
+def require(test, message):
+    global checks
+    checks+=1
+    if not test:raise RuntimeError(message)
+
+S=frozenset((1,2,4,8,15))
+spaces={frozenset((0,))}
+pending=list(spaces)
+while pending:
+    H=pending.pop()
+    for x in range(16):
+        K=H|frozenset(h^x for h in H)
+        if K not in spaces:spaces.add(K);pending.append(K)
+require(len(spaces)==67,'four-bit vector-space lattice')
+for H in spaces:
+    require(0 in H and all(a^b in H for a in H for b in H),'subspace closure')
+for size in range(1,5):
+    for subset in itertools.combinations(S,size):
+        require(__import__('functools').reduce(int.__xor__,subset,0)!=0,'proper circuit relation')
+require(__import__('functools').reduce(int.__xor__,S,0)==0,'five-character circuit')
+
+options=sorted((H for H in spaces if len(H)<=11),key=lambda H:(len(H),tuple(sorted(H))))
+families=[];all_families=0
+def search(start,cost,chosen,cover):
+    global all_families
+    all_families+=1
+    if S<=cover:families.append(tuple(chosen))
+    for i in range(start,len(options)):
+        H=options[i]
+        if cost+len(H)>11:continue
+        search(i+1,cost+len(H),chosen+[H],cover|(H&S))
+search(0,0,[],frozenset())
+require(len(families)==52,'all budget-eleven target-cover families')
+patterns=collections.Counter()
+for fam in families:
+    patterns[tuple(sorted(len(H) for H in fam))]+=1
+    nontrivial=[H for H in fam if len(H)>1]
+    require(all(len(H) in (2,4) for H in nontrivial),'no degree-eight target cover')
+    require(sum(len(H) for H in nontrivial)==10,'target-carrying degree')
+    for chi in S:
+        require(sum(chi in H for H in fam)==1,'target character assigned once')
+    for H in nontrivial:
+        active=H&S
+        require(len(active)==len(H)//2,'optimal character density')
+        for chi in H-{0}-S:
+            require(sum(chi in K for K in fam)==1,'auxiliary character cannot cancel')
+    require(sum(len(H&S) for H in nontrivial)==5,'mass lower coefficient')
+
+def chi(a,g):return 1 if (a&g).bit_count()%2==0 else -1
+
+# Verify the separate orbit decoders and the exact cancellation on all 16 inputs.
+for g in range(16):
+    signs=[chi(a,g) for a in (1,2,4,8,15)]
+    require(__import__('functools').reduce(int.__mul__,signs,1)==1,'circuit character product')
+    indicator=Q((signs[0]==1 and signs[1]==1))
+    majority=Q(sum(x==1 for x in signs[2:])>=2)
+    target=Q(3,8)+sum(map(Q,signs))/8
+    require((indicator+majority)/2==target,'degree-four plus degree-eight cancellation')
+    require(target in (Q(0),Q(1,2),Q(1)),'probability boundary values')
+    for t in (Q(0),Q(1,7),Q(3,5),Q(4,5),Q(1)):
+        mixed=Q(3,8)+t*sum(map(Q,signs))/8
+        require(0<=mixed<=1,'contrast probability')
+        decoder_a=(1-t)*Q(3,8)+t*indicator
+        decoder_b=(1-t)*Q(3,8)+t*majority
+        require(0<=decoder_a<=1 and 0<=decoder_b<=1,'upper realization decoder bounds')
+        require((decoder_a+decoder_b)/2==mixed,'all-word contrast realization')
+        if t<=Q(3,5):
+            small=[Q(3,8)+Q(5,8)*t*s for s in signs]
+            require(all(0<=x<=1 for x in small),'degree-ten decoder bounds')
+            require(sum(small)/5==mixed,'degree-ten response equality')
+
+# Module rank and residual cardinality from character independence / direct tables.
+matrix=[[chi(a,g) for a in (0,1,2,4,8,15)] for g in range(16)]
+for i in range(6):
+    for j in range(6):
+        require(sum(row[i]*row[j] for row in matrix)==(16 if i==j else 0),'character orthogonality')
+residuals={tuple(Q(3,8)+sum(Q(chi(a,g^h),8) for a in S) for h in range(16)) for g in range(16)}
+require(len(residuals)==16,'six-dimensional response has sixteen residuals')
+
+# Independently reconstruct the family-specific signed scores used in the
+# robust corollary. W is an annihilator (a space of characters); its primal
+# stabilizer consists of group elements on which every character in W is one.
+expected_histograms={
+    0:{-4:1,0:10,4:5},
+    1:{-3:1,-1:6,1:4,3:2,5:3},
+    2:{-2:5,0:4,2:2,4:4,6:1},
+}
+expected_norms={0:Q(3,2),1:Q(17,8),2:Q(9,4)}
+distinct_partitions=set()
+for fam in families:
+    pairs=tuple(sorted(tuple(sorted(W&S)) for W in fam if len(W)==4))
+    distinct_partitions.add(pairs)
+    z={g:1-sum(chi(a,g) for a in S)
+         +sum(chi(a^b,g) for a,b in pairs) for g in range(16)}

+## 1. Headline live/terminal subtraction
+
+We agree with the exact mathematical issue identified by the referee. A lower on live labels does not imply a lower on their disjoint union with output labels. The retained R57 repair, now built and preserved in full, defines two primitive interfaces before their minimax values: a state-only absorbing halt map, and a transition-emitted terminal event. Theorem `thm:main`, Lemma `lem:packing`, the heralding example, both Gaussian results and the joint-error theorem all retain the appropriate width. With matched effort, mandatory and sufficient B live roles, and identity exports, the exact widths are M-B for state stopping and M for event stopping. We do not quietly forbid the reviewer's two-label construction.
+
+This part is inherited from R57 source, not new R58 mathematics. The new theorem uses its live lower at the actual witness and never obtains a state count from the comparison process.
+
+## 2. Dependence on an exact admitted reference
+
+The report correctly identifies the strength of requiring one exact admitted reference law under every legal action and history. R57 removed exactness only from the upper construction. R58 removes the exact-membership requirement from the converse as well, subject to explicit productive-row and actual-occupation certificates.
+
+The new center is `thm:reference-stability`. A positive prepared comparison experiment may lie outside the operating uncertainty family. At a single actual witness, each full productive report–audit row is close in mass and squared-task measures to the corresponding comparison row. Lemma `lem:comparison-submeasure` integrates those comparison rows against the actual pre-call occupation and the actual acceptance/readout rule. The resulting positive submeasure has mass in [1-a_N,1+a_N], is dominated by actual productive count times the comparison preparation law, and has controlled task discrepancy. It is expressly not claimed to be the terminal law of an admissible comparison execution. Normalizing it without paying for missing mass would be wrong.
+
+For t=(1-a_N)_+, this gives `[t Q_m(b_-/t)-e_N]_+` as an all-program lower. An independent common approximate construction gives `(1+b_+ a_+) Q_m(b_+/(1+b_+a_+))+b_+e_+` at the same physical budget. No equality of the two effort constants, whole-path coupling, minimax interchange, or termination under the comparison model is presumed. Corollary `cor:reference-geometry` states precisely the error regime preserving matching acquired-geometry rates. It does not silently extend a fixed nonzero calibration error to unlimited resolution.
+
+## 3. Nonuniform and singular content
+
+Theorem `thm:metastable` proves, rather than merely names, a nonuniform extension. Bad-mode errors can remain order one, mode residence times can be long, and observations and stopping can select the mode. The bound retains actual initial bad mass divided by exit probability and the controlled entry-to-exit ratio times actual raw cost. A killed nonnegative potential proves the uniform all-strategy occupation bound. It is an analytic certificate, not a free observer register.
+
+The two new raw verification theorems use a classical sign channel and a noncommuting positive qubit instrument. Their reference preparations can be biased/near-mixed rather than exactly fair. Imperfect randomization and unnormalized instrument errors are certified directly. Rank-one outcomes and continuous/atomic mixtures are permitted without normalizing a small-probability posterior. A hidden calibration mode gives concrete positive metastable examples of each. Nominal acquired geometry and actual perturbed support are never identified without the transfer error.
+
+## 4. Joint resources and one scored task
+
+Corollary `cor:calibrated-joint` combines the two-sided imperfect-reference bounds with the inherited early-erasure and invisible calibration-sign task. The lower contributions hold under the same actual witness and indistinguishable sign mixture. The attained deficiency is exactly epsilon because the virtual bit must be delivered before the core. Initial observation and terminal audit cost two additional calls; the seven live tagged roles and output-copy counts are explicit. These are sufficient constructions, not unproved minimality claims.
+
+Proposition `prop:calibrated-numerics` propagates uniformly certified acceptance and exported-readout errors through the same conditional-hazard argument, adjusting the design cap before execution. It does not infer effective computation from Borel measurability. Complete stopped-law simulator errors are different from productive-row errors; reverse risk transfer needs a reverse resource certificate or a direct witness. Continuing simulator states, terminal export classes, program bits, workspace and physical time remain separate.
+
+## 5. Natural nonintervening application and literature
+
+The entire R57 directional Gaussian proof is retained: all-strategy radial reliability lower, independent worst static-direction covering lower, one common radial-waiting upper, exact m<=d obstruction, fixed-width limit and ratio-one noise scale. The raw target is unchanged. We do not relabel that inherited result as a new R58 application or as the resolution of a named external open problem.
+
+The introduction keeps the exact trimmed-population normalization and 1997/1999 primary literature, and adds the September 2026 version of Hansson–Wahlberg on occupation-weighted rollout error. Drift telescoping, transient occupation error accumulation, and the expected-time amplification principle are expressly standard. The proposed new mathematical combination is the accepted comparison submeasure with missing-mass and task control, the resulting all-program finite-dictionary lower at a nonadmitted comparison, and its same-budget common upper and fully priced stopping interfaces. This is a priority positioning, not an independent priority certificate.
+
+## 6. Scope, writing and verification
+
+The main theorem is stated before its exact special case and realizations. We retain the General Theta title and the G1/G3 mother problem; the manuscript is not a survey or a replacement realization paper. Older proofs and all R57 responses remain available in full. +#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Finite witnesses and numerical consistency checks, never mathematical proof.
+All checks raise explicitly and run identically with Python -O.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+from fractions import Fraction as F
+from itertools import product
+import hashlib, json, math
+
+COUNTS: dict[str,int] = {}
+DIGEST: list[str] = []
+def check(group: str, condition: bool, message: str, value=None) -> None:
+    if not condition:
+        raise RuntimeError(f'{group}: {message}')
+    COUNTS[group] = COUNTS.get(group,0)+1
+    if value is not None:
+        DIGEST.append(repr(value))
+
+def main() -> None:
+    # Independent live/output injections, including the reviewer's two-label gate.
+    for live,term in product(range(1,18),repeat=2):
+        event=max(live,term); typed=live+term
+        live_ids=set(range(live)); term_ids=set(range(term))
+        check('exact_role_packing',len(live_ids|term_ids)==event,'event union')
+        check('exact_role_packing',len(live_ids)+len(set(range(live,typed)))==typed,'typed disjoint')
+        check('exact_role_packing',live+term-len(live_ids&term_ids)==event,'overlap identity',(live,term,event,typed))
+        for cap in range(0, min(live,term)+1):
+            needed=live+term-cap
+            check('exact_partial_overlap',term<=needed-max(live-cap,0),'terminal cap')
+    # Both terminal readouts may overlap the gate and productive command labels.
+    commands={0:'gate',1:'productive'}; readout={0:F(-1),1:F(1)}
+    transitions={('gate',False):(0,0),('gate',True):(1,0),('productive','reject'):(0,0),('productive','negative'):(0,1),('productive','positive'):(1,1)}
+    for key,(state,halt) in transitions.items():
+        check('exact_two_label_gate',state in commands and state in readout,'shared label')
+        if halt:check('exact_two_label_gate',key[0]=='productive','no gate commitment')
+    check('exact_two_label_gate',len(commands)==2 and len(readout)==2,'two live and two output roles')
+    # The exact budget substitution and the special first-attempt boundary.
+    for den in range(2,25):
+        a=F(1,den)
+        for b in range(2,30):
+            if F(b)<1/(1-a):continue
+            beta=F(b)/(1+b*a)
+            check('exact_approximate_budget',beta>=1 and beta*a<1,'admissible design')
+            check('exact_approximate_budget',beta/(1-beta*a)==b,'physical budget exactly restored',beta)
+            for q,e in ((F(0),F(1,100)),(F(1,5),F(1,60)),(F(2,3),F(0))):
+                check('exact_approximate_budget',(q+beta*e)/(1-beta*a)==(1+b*a)*q+b*e,'loss substitution')
+    for b in range(1,50):
+        e=F(1,100*b);p=F(1,b)
+        check('exact_sharp_task_defect',b*e*p==e and b*e<=1,'raw loss measure defect',b*e)
+        for r in (F(-1),F(-1,3),F(0),F(2,3),F(1)):
+            v=b*e+r*r
+            check('exact_sharp_task_defect',v>=b*e,'conditional variance converse')
+        check('exact_sharp_task_defect',p*b==1,'selected mass and paid cost')
+    for beta in range(2,30):
+        for den in (2,3,5,11):
+            a=F(1,beta*den);p=F(1,beta)-a
+            check('exact_sharp_waiting',1/p==F(beta)/(1-beta*a),'waiting denominator',1/p)
+    for r in (F(-1),F(-3,7),F(0),F(2,5),F(1)):
+        check('exact_no_first_moment_balance',((1-r)**2+(-1-r)**2)/2==1+r*r,'all-program indistinguishability')
+    for M in range(7,500):
+        m=M//3
+        check('exact_joint_roles',max(7,3*m)<=M and 4*m>=M,'event joint construction')
+        if M>=13:
+            k=(M-1)//3-2
+            check('exact_joint_roles',7+3*k<=M and 8*k>=M,'typed joint construction')
+    for l,t,K,E in product(range(1,7),repeat=4):
+        check('exact_simulator_roles',max(l*K,t*E)<=l*K+t*E,'packed versus typed composition')
+    for l,t,k1,k2,e1,e2 in product(range(1,4),repeat=6):
+        check('exact_simulator_associativity',((l*k1)*k2,(t*e1)*e2)==(l*(k1*k2),t*(e1*e2)),'pair products')
+    # Probabilistic raw moment perturbations through sign and Pauli controls.
+    import numpy as np
+    I=np.eye(2,dtype=complex);X=np.array([[0,1],[1,0]],complex)
+    Y=np.array([[0,-1j],[1j,0]],complex);Z=np.diag([1.,-1.]).astype(complex)
+    pauli=[I,X,Y,Z]
+    for fault in (0.,.01,.1,.24):
+        weights=np.array([.25+fault,.25-fault,.25,.25])
+        for vec in ([0,0,0],[1,0,0],[0,0,1],[.2,.3,.4]):
+            rho=(I+vec[0]*X+vec[1]*Y+vec[2]*Z)/2
+            out=sum(w*(u@rho@u.conj().T) for w,u in zip(weights,pauli))
+            trdist=np.sum(np.abs(np.linalg.eigvalsh(out-I/2)))/2
+            check('numeric_raw_perturbation',trdist<=fault+1e-13,'Pauli total variation certificate')
+        ref=sum(w*(u@(I/2)@u.conj().T) for w,u in zip(weights,pauli))
+        check('numeric_raw_perturbation',np.linalg.norm(ref-I/2)<1e-13,'same reference remains exact')
+    # Directional posterior integrals are independently compared to scaled Bessel ratios.
+    from scipy.integrate import quad
+    from scipy.special import ive
+    for d in (2,3,4,7,12):
+        exponent=(d-3)/2
+        for s in (.05,.3,1.,3.,10.,50.):
+            # quad's algebraic endpoint rule handles d=2 without endpoint division.
+            den=quad(lambda z:math.exp(s*(z-1)),-1,1,weight='alg',wvar=(exponent,exponent),epsabs=2e-12,epsrel=2e-12)[0]
+            num=quad(lambda z:z*math.exp(s*(z-1)),-1,1,weight='alg',wvar=(exponent,exponent),epsabs=2e-12,epsrel=2e-12)[0]
+            A=num/den;ratio=ive(d/2,s)/ive(d/2-1,s)
+            check('numeric_directional_moments',abs(A-ratio)<2e-10,'independent axial integration')
+            check('numeric_directional_moments',0<=A<=1 and 1-A*A<=2*(1-A)+2e-15<=2*(1-A*A)+2e-14,'D/U pointwise bounds')
+        s=100000.
+        A=ive(d/2,s)/ive(d/2-1,s)
+        check('numeric_directional_moments',abs(2*s*(1-A)/(d-1)-1)<3e-5,'posterior leading constant')
+    # Deterministic simplex covering witness: exhaustive rational directions in R^d.
+    for d in (2,3,4,5):
+        P=np.eye(d+1)-np.ones((d+1,d+1))/(d+1)
+        verts=P*math.sqrt((d+1)/d)
+        check('numeric_simplex_cover',np.max(np.abs(np.sum(verts*verts,axis=1)-1))<1e-13,'unit vertices')
+        for j in range(1,80):
+            u=np.sin(np.arange(1,d+2)*j*.73);u-=u.mean();u/=np.linalg.norm(u)
+            dots=verts@u
+            check('numeric_simplex_cover',dots.max()>=1/d-1e-13,'inradius support')
+            dist=((verts/d-u)**2).sum(axis=1).min()
+            check('numeric_simplex_cover',dist<=1-1/d**2+1e-13,'d+1 interior centers')
+    counts=dict(sorted(COUNTS.items()))
+    print(json.dumps({'status':'PASS','counts':counts,'exact_checks':sum(v for k,v in counts.items() if k.startswith('exact_')),'floating_checks':sum(v for k,v in counts.items() if k.startswith('numeric_')),'witness_sha256':hashlib.sha256('\n'.join(DIGEST).encode()).hexdigest(),'limitations':'finite witnesses and floating consistency only; all continuous claims require the manuscript proofs'},sort_keys=True,indent=2))
+
+if __name__=='__main__':main()"},{"sha":"762ec9d6d164d7b229b6a4cd45a2a523498818d3","filename":"papers/General-Theta-Foundations-I-restart/r74-positive-memory-structure/companion-r58/main.tex","status":"added","additions":59,"deletions":0,"changes":59,"blob_url":"https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/theta-theory/blob/29b999abf11c43709e64be58765aa1984d13ac91/papers%2FGeneral-Theta-Foundations-I-restart%2Fr74-positive-memory-structure%2Fcompanion-r58%2Fmain.tex","raw_url":"https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/theta-theory/raw/29b999abf11c43709e64be58765aa1984d13ac91/papers%2FGeneral-Theta-Foundations-I-restart%2Fr74-positive-memory-structure%2Fcompanion-r58%2Fmain.tex","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/TrillionniumFoundation/theta-theory/contents/papers%2FGeneral-Theta-Foundations-I-restart%2Fr74-positive-memory-structure%2Fcompanion-r58%2Fmain.tex?ref=29b999abf11c43709e64be58765aa1984d13ac91","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@

+\begin{document}
+\begin{abstract}
+We study finite-resource prediction in positive prepared causal experiments using an actually prepared comparison law that need not belong to the operating model family. A reference-side converse replaces only each productive report--audit row while retaining the actual pre-call occupation. The resulting positive submeasure has controlled missing mass, a cost-certified density cap and controlled task moments, giving a lower bound uniform over all legal strategies. A common parameter-independent approximate balancing program gives a matching upper at the same expected physical budget. The bounds recover exact stopped risk profiles at zero error and matching acquired-geometry orders on a quantified two-sided calibration regime. Drift certificates extend the converse to metastable and singular calibration with explicit preparation mass and residence time. Classical controlled channels and noncommuting quantum instruments verify the same theorem without an exactly fair operating reference or a posterior-rank floor. A same-task extension combines attained calibration and causal erasure error. Event-stopped observers may reuse live labels for outputs, whereas intrinsically state-stopped observers pay for disjoint live and terminal roles; both resource laws are proved. We retain nonintervening Gaussian sensing with a joint waiting--output geometry. Numerical precision, program description, workspace, physical time and simulator states are accounted for separately.
+\end{abstract}

+\section{Introduction}
+A prepared causal experiment determines which future tests can be predicted from its reports. The predictive quotient records this equivalence of executable tests, but does not by itself determine the geometry that a finite observer can acquire. Waiting for a rare informative report changes both the attainable law and the physical cost. Persistent memory constrains the route to that report as well as its final description. A further difficulty is calibration: a comparison law may describe a physically prepared ideal experiment accurately without being an exact member of the operating model family. A converse that silently treats it as an admitted model is then unjustified.
+
+We establish a two-sided resource--risk transfer under explicit raw experiment certificates. One actual witness bounds the effort of every competing strategy and the accumulated discrepancy of its productive report--audit rows from a prepared comparison law. Separately, one parameter-independent acquisition program approximately balances the report and task measures in every operating model. Our center is Theorem~\ref{thm:reference-stability}. It uses neither an exact comparison model in the uncertainty family nor a comparison execution that stops under the competing program.
+
+The main construction in the converse is an accepted comparison submeasure. Retain the actual distribution of each pre-call history, but replace its current productive report--audit row only. The resulting positive measure has a controlled mass defect and a density cap set by actual expected acquisition count. It need not be an executable terminal law. Its unnormalized task moments nevertheless give an all-strategy risk lower. This separates a valid local comparison from the generally invalid replacement of an entire selected path law.
+
+Write $\Qm_m(b)$ for the marked trimmed-quantization profile derived from the comparison's report law $\nu$, audit mean $f$, and residual variance $w$; its cap $b$ retains actual preparation mass. In the matched-effort, identity-export case the central bounds take the form
+\[
+ \left[t\Qm_m(b/t)-\mathfrak e_N\right]_+
+ \ \le R\ \le
+ (1+ba_+)\Qm_m\!\left(\frac b{1+ba_+}\right)+be_+,
+ \qquad t=(1-\mathfrak a_N)_+.
+\]
+Here the lower is read as zero at $t=0$, and the upper has its stated feasibility threshold. The lower defect bounds are actual accumulated charges, not a best-policy occupation estimate. Different effort constants and export multiplicities remain explicitly distinct in the theorem. The formula recovers exact equalities at zero errors and matching geometric orders on a quantitative two-sided calibration regime.
+
+The output width depends on the physical stopping convention. A state-stopped observer has a state-only halt map; its live and terminal labels are disjoint, giving width $M-B$ when $B$ live labels are mandatory and sufficient. An event-stopped observer emits its final commitment during a transition and may reuse live labels as final outputs, giving width $M$. We retain both exact resource laws and their proof, rather than excluding reuse silently. All intercall phases, clocks and continuing random seeds are charged.
+
+Theorem~\ref{thm:metastable} replaces small uniform defects by a drift certificate on actual good/bad mode occupation. The initial bad mass and its residence time appear explicitly; singular and changing-rank report kernels are permitted. Theorems~\ref{thm:classical-calibrated} and \ref{thm:quantum-calibrated} verify the same central theorem from a classical controlled sign channel and a noncommuting positive quantum instrument. Their nominal balanced preparations need not be operating models. A joint calibration--erasure extension keeps all errors in the same terminal squared loss, while finite numerical execution and causal simulator costs are stated separately.
+
+We also retain a different, nonintervening raw application. A current hidden unit vector is observed through Gaussian noise and is not altered by the observer. Theorem~\ref{thm:directional} proves a matching law
+\[
+ (1+\log b)^{-1/2}+m^{-2/(d-1)}
+\]
+against every legal stopping rule, together with exact finite-output obstructions and a sharp noise constant. This application is not mislabeled as a post-command balanced task, and its physical posterior is derived directly from the Gaussian kernel.
+
+The variational profile itself has an established ancestry. When $w=0$, writing $a=1/b$ and $g=h/b$ gives $0\le g\le1$, $\int g\,d\nu=a$, and the objective is the normalized distortion of a fractionally retained mass $a$. This is the population trimming formulation underlying trimmed $k$-means and impartial trimming \cite{CGM97}, \cite{GG99}. With $w\ne0$ it is the corresponding marked objective. We do not claim the density cap or low-distortion selection principle as new. Classical reject-option prediction \cite{Chow}, \cite{DHZ}, invariant decision procedures \cite{Luschgy}, and quantum randomization \cite{AMTW} supply related tools. Approximate rejection sampling from a fixed independent batch \cite{BP23}, \cite{SPJ26} has a different budget and output objective: here physical attempts can be history dependent, the criterion is an audited decision loss, and a single finite-state program must work for every admitted model.
+
+Almost-sure expected-cost reachability in partially observed control is studied in \cite{CCGK}, and fixed-memory limit-sure reachability in \cite{ACSS}. Sufficiency results for chattering policies in absorbing decision processes are developed in \cite{DPChatter}. These works concern policy classes and reachability or occupation criteria; the present matching assertions require, in addition, the specified report--audit balance and acquisition certificates.
+
+
+Accumulation of local error along transient occupation and Lyapunov telescoping are standard stochastic-control techniques. In particular, the occupation-weighted rollout bounds of Hansson and Wahlberg \cite{HW26} address policy-specific Bellman approximation and properness. We do not claim occupation weighting, drift control, or the mere appearance of an expected-time factor as new. Here the comparison submeasure controls both its lost mass and its task moment against a trimmed finite-dictionary optimum, yielding a converse uniform over all admissible observers even when the comparison process is not an admitted or terminating execution. This combines a different quantifier structure, a selected geometric objective and explicit stopping-resource widths.
+
+The result is a sufficient-class theorem, not a classification of all positive kernels. Measurable quotient realization has its separate hypotheses in Appendix~\ref{sec:quotient}; arbitrary projective arrays are not declared physical states. Our proofs distinguish new comparison arguments from inherited exact balance and role counting, and from standard conditional projection, compactness, trimming, Gaussian tails and covering. Ideal Borel existence is not finite algorithmic synthesis. +\section{Prepared experiments and stopping resources}
+\label{sec:experiment}
+All state, action and report spaces are standard Borel. An unknown index $\theta\in\Theta$ specifies a prepared law and positive normalized causal kernels (positivity means nonnegative measures, not a strictly positive density at every report). It is fixed for an entire execution; it may index an arbitrary history-dependent physical evolution. Policies see only past reports, legal physical commands and their own allowed coins. They never see $\theta$. All assertions below are for the declared experiment and test, not for a formal parameter manifold.
+
+A call has a nonnegative cost bounded below by $c_*>0$. A predictable flag declares whether the call is productive. Commitment is allowed only after a productive report. Conditional on commitment, a fixed bounded future audit $Z\in H$ is executed, where $H\subset\R^k$ is compact and convex. This audit is not observed before the prediction is committed. The loss is $\|Z-r\|^2$, $r\in H$. Each productive call has a potential audit specified by the same kernel, whether or not the observer commits there. A fresh stopping coin is independent of that audit conditional on the current physical report and history. All other informative components of the current report must be included in the conditional laws below.
+
+The cost $N$ in the core theorem counts preparation, failed gate calls, productive calls, and all calls preceding commitment. A separately required final physical audit has its own explicit cost. Thus a protocol with one initial preparation call and one final audit uses total raw budget $N+2$, not $N$. Time, bit operations and scratch space are not identified with raw-call count.
+
+\subsection*{The stopping interface and retained labels}
+A checkpoint procedure may retain the entire precommit history, but its committed value belongs to one fixed dictionary of at most $m$ elements. This convention counts only its terminal dictionary, not its full-history working memory. Its physical acquisition and audit costs are still charged.
+
+A finite-state observer has an alphabet $S$ of at most $M$ labels and one fixed parameter-independent program. At every intercall boundary its only observer memory is the retained label. Its next physical command distribution is a fixed function of that label. In particular, the physical port identity, elapsed time, prior report and subprogram index are not additional free inputs. During a call the current command, its report and fresh independent coins are available; the post-report transition can depend on them. No such coin, report, real register or clock persists unless encoded in $S$. A fixed terminal decoder $r:S\to H$ reads only the committed label; it never reads the report or the audit. The two stopping interfaces are as follows.
+
+\begin{definition}[Event and state stopping]\label{def:stopping}
+In the \emph{event-stopped} interface, a post-report kernel emits $(s',e)\in S\times\{0,1\}$. The value $e=1$ is permitted only after a productive call and commits exactly once: the experiment stops, the label $s'$ is retained, and the decoder returns $r(s')$. No next command is executed. The commitment event belongs to the public stopped transcript; it is not an extra stored bit available during subsequent computation. On branches with $e=0$, execution continues at $s'$. A label may therefore be used both live and terminal on different branches.
+
+In the \emph{state-stopped} interface there is instead a fixed map $h_*:S\to\{0,1\}$. The initial label has type zero. A transition commits if and only if $h_*(s')=1$, and entry into type one is permitted only after a productive report. Type-one labels are globally terminal and absorbing: they have no executed command row. Type-zero labels are live. The halt status is thus completely determined by the retained state, and live and terminal labels are disjoint.
+\end{definition}
+
+Let $L_\gamma$ be the set of labels reached before physical calls and $T_\gamma$ the set reached on commitment, under the relevant family of path laws. The program's role counts are $\ell_\gamma=|L_\gamma|$ and $t_\gamma=|T_\gamma|$, with overlap $o_\gamma=|L_\gamma\cap T_\gamma|$. Its actual alphabet count is $\ell_\gamma+t_\gamma-o_\gamma$, whereas its number of distinct decoder values is at most $t_\gamma$. A mandatory lower on $\ell_\gamma$ does not imply a subtraction from $M$ unless overlap is excluded. This is the distinction used below, not an unmentioned memory convention.
+
+Under robust almost-sure commitment and robust expected core cost at most $N$, write the infimal worst-case risks as $R_\cp^\Theta(N,m)$, $R_\evt^\Theta(N,M)$ and $R_\st^\Theta(N,M)$. +\section{Proof of the transfer and physical memory bounds}
+\begin{lemma}[Attainment and continuity of the acquired profile]\label{lem:attain}
+The minimum in \eqref{eq:profile} is attained. For each fixed $m$, $\Qm_m$ is nonincreasing and left-continuous on $(1,\infty)$.
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+Represent a dictionary by an ordered $m$-tuple in the compact space $H^m$, permitting repetitions. The feasible densities are a weak-star compact subset of the radius-$b$ ball of $L^\infty(\nu)$: positivity, the upper bound and the mass equality are weak-star closed. Nets suffice; no unmentioned sequential compactness is used. The bounded loss functions vary uniformly continuously with the tuple, since squared distance on $H$ is uniformly Lipschitz in its second argument. Along a convergent product net, split the objective difference into this uniform difference and the weak-star pairing with one fixed bounded measurable loss. This proves attainment. Monotonicity is immediate. If $h$ is optimal at $b>1$, use $h_\lambda=(1-\lambda)h+\lambda$, whose cap is $b_\lambda=(1-\lambda)b+\lambda<b$. Its loss tends to the optimal loss as $\lambda\downarrow0$. Monotonicity sandwiches the values and proves the last assertion.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{lemma}[A terminal measure obtained by any competitor]\label{lem:lower}
+Under $\theta_0$, every legal procedure committing exactly once, almost surely, of expected cost at most $N$ has a terminal mark measure $\zeta$ satisfying
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:dominated-terminal}
+ \zeta(X)=1,\qquad
+ 0\le\zeta\le (\E_{\theta_0}A_\tau)\nu\le (N/\kappa_-)\nu.
+\end{equation}
+If its terminal dictionary is $C$, its expected loss is at least $\int d_C\,d\zeta$, where $d_C=w+\operatorname{dist}(f,C)^2$.

+For a Borel set $D$, predictability of productive calls and the conditional reference row imply, by Tonelli,
+\[
+ \E_{\theta_0}\sum_{t\le\tau}\one_{\{t\text{ productive}\}}\one_{\{X_t\in D\}}
+   =\E_{\theta_0}A_\tau\,\nu(D).

+The terminal report is one of these reports, so its measure is dominated by this acquired report-count measure. Almost-sure commitment gives mass one, and \eqref{eq:effort} gives the last inequality. Only now take its Radon--Nikodym density, choosing a Borel version clipped to the displayed cap.

+\begin{lemma}[Exact packing of live and output roles]\label{lem:packing}

The next command row is used only on continuing branches, and the decoder only after commitment. Thus their tables may share a label without conflict. No mode bit is stored: the event ends execution before any further command. Coupling the original and recoded within-call coins proves equality of every finite prefix and of the stopped transcript; almost-sure commitment completes the latter assertion. A label always has one fixed terminal decoder value, proving the converse dictionary bound. +\section{The two-sided causal transfer theorem}
+\label{sec:reference-stability}
+For an interface $\iota\in\{\cp,\evt,\st\}$ write $R_\iota(N,M)$ for the risks of Section~\ref{sec:experiment}. Suppose every terminating state-stopped competitor needs at least $B_0\ge1$ live labels at $\theta_*$. Let
+\[
+ m_-(M)=
+ \begin{cases}M,&\iota=\cp,\evt,\\M-B_0,&\iota=\st,\end{cases}
+ \quad
+ m_+(M)=
+ \begin{cases}\lfloor M/D_0\rfloor,&\iota=\cp,\evt,\\
+ \lfloor(M-B)/D_0\rfloor,&\iota=\st.
+ \end{cases}
+\]
+For the event upper additionally require $M\ge B$. If no stronger live lower is known, $B_0=1$ is always valid for a procedure initially waiting to make a physical call.
+
+\begin{theorem}[Calibration-stable causal acquired-geometry transfer]
+\label{thm:reference-stability}
+Assume precisely the experiment, row, effort, occupation and construction certificates of Sections~\ref{sec:experiment}--\ref{sec:calibrated}; an exactly matching reference model in $\Theta$ is \emph{not} assumed. Fix $N$ and $M$ with $b_-=N/\kappa_-\ge1$ and $m_-(M)\ge1$. Put $t_N=(1-\mathfrak a_N)_+$. If $t_N>0$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:reference-lower}
+ R_\iota(N,M)\ge
+ \left[t_N\Qm_{m_-(M)}(b_-/t_N)-\mathfrak e_N\right]_+.
+\end{equation}
+When $t_N=0$, the asserted lower is zero, with no evaluation of $\Qm$ at infinity. An empty legal class has risk $+\infty$ and is not made feasible by this formula.
+
+For $m_+(M)\ge1$, the stated event feasibility condition, and
+$b_+=N/\kappa_+\ge(1-a_+)^{-1}$, one common Borel program at the \emph{same} budget $N$ attains an upper bound
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:reference-upper}
+ R_\iota(N,M)\le
+ (1+b_+a_+)\Qm_{m_+(M)}\!\left(\frac{b_+}{1+b_+a_+}\right)+b_+e_+.
+\end{equation}
+It commits almost surely, with at most $B$ live and $D_0m_+(M)$ output roles. For $1\le b_+<(1-a_+)^{-1}$ replace the right side by $\Qm_{m_+(M)}(1)+e_+$ using first-attempt commitment.
+
+In particular, with uniform lower defects $a_-,e_-$ and $b_-a_-<1$, the lower reads
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:uniform-reference-lower}
+ \left[(1-b_-a_-)\Qm_{m_-(M)}
+       \!\left(\frac{b_-}{1-b_-a_-}\right)-b_-e_-\right]_+.
+\end{equation}
+At zero defects these inequalities recover the exact role-dependent identities of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} whenever effort, live counts and identity exports match. The lower ranges over all legal strategies; the upper is one program for the entire actual model family.
+\end{theorem}
+
+The proof uses comparison rows along \emph{actual} histories. A product coupling of whole stopped paths would require a separate termination and cost comparison and is not used.

+\begin{lemma}[Accepted comparison submeasure]\label{lem:comparison-submeasure}
+Fix a legal competing procedure with committed outputs in a fixed dictionary $C\subset H$, $|C|\le m$, and finite actual expected cost. Under the lower certificates, there are finite measures $\xi_c$ on $X$, $c\in C$, such that, for $\xi=\sum_c\xi_c$,
+\begin{align}
+ \xi&\le (\E_*A_\tau)\nu,\label{eq:phantom-cap}\\
+ |\xi(X)-1|&\le\mathfrak a_N,\label{eq:phantom-mass}\\
+ \E_*\|Z-\widehat r\|^2
+ &\ge\sum_{c\in C}\int d_c(x)\xi_c(dx)-\mathfrak e_N.
+ \label{eq:phantom-risk}
+\end{align}
+The measures need not be terminal laws of any comparison process.
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+Represent each current random transition by an independent uniform variable on $[0,1]$, using the standard Borel kernel representation. Absorb it into the current report on both sides. Fix a reached productive history and the chosen command. The transition supplies an acceptance probability $q_h(y)\in[0,1]$ and, on its acceptance event, a finite-image readout $r_h(y)\in C$. Equivalently one may use the acceptance indicator with the adjoined uniform variable. Complete $r_h$ arbitrarily on rejection. Conditioning also on current command coins causes no loss: \eqref{eq:row-mass}--\eqref{eq:row-loss} hold for every chosen legal command.
+
+For Borel $D\subset X$, define
+\[
+ \xi_c(D)=\E_*\sum_{i\le\tau:\ i\ {\rm productive}}
+  \int\one_{\{\pi_{H_{i-1},a_i}(y)\in D\}}
+       q_{H_{i-1}}(y)\one_{\{r_{H_{i-1}}(y)=c\}}
+       P^0_{H_{i-1},a_i}(dy,H).
+\]
+The expectation is over actual pre-call histories and commands; it does not replace their distribution. All integrands are jointly measurable, so Tonelli defines finite measures. Summing over $c$ and dropping $q_h\le1$ gives \eqref{eq:phantom-cap}, since every comparison row has mark law $\nu$. Actual commitment occurs exactly once almost surely. Its corresponding sum of actual conditional acceptance probabilities therefore has expectation one. Subtract the two sums, apply \eqref{eq:row-mass} termwise, and use \eqref{eq:defect-occupation}, obtaining \eqref{eq:phantom-mass}.
+
+On the actual disjoint commitment events the expected terminal losses sum to the risk. Replace only the current report--audit row in each contribution. The sum of absolute errors is at most $\mathfrak e_N$. By \eqref{eq:row-moments}, the replaced conditional contribution is precisely $d_{r_h(y)}(\pi y)$. This proves \eqref{eq:phantom-risk}. One may first truncate the number of calls; nonnegativity and the finite accumulated defect bounds justify passage to the limit. The comparison process need neither stop under this program nor satisfy its budget.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:reference-stability}]
+For the lower fix any admissible competitor. Its actual number of distinct outputs is at most $m_-(M)$: checkpoint and event-stopped procedures have at most $M$, whereas intrinsic state stopping leaves at most $M-B_0$ because its live and terminal alphabets are disjoint. This is a statement about its actual state labels, not about a fictitious comparison execution.
+
+Use Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison-submeasure} with its fixed dictionary. If $t_N>0$, put $t=\xi(X)\ge t_N$ and $\xi'=(t_N/t)\xi$. Then $\xi'$ has mass $t_N$, and $\xi'\le b_-\nu$ by the actual effort certificate. Thus $h=(d\xi'/d\nu)/t_N$ is a probability density with cap $b_-/t_N$. Nonnegativity of squared loss and nearest-dictionary projection give
+\[
+ \sum_c\int d_c\,d\xi_c
+ \ge\int\bigl[w+\operatorname{dist}(f,C)^2\bigr]d\xi
+ \ge t_N\Qm_{m_-(M)}(b_-/t_N).
+\]
+Combine this with \eqref{eq:phantom-risk}, use nonnegativity, take the worst case over actual models, and then the infimum over all competitors. No minimax interchange or comparison-model membership is involved.
+
+For the upper take an attained dictionary and density at cap
+$\beta=b_+/(1+b_+a_+)\ge1$, and accept the virtual mark with probability $h/\beta$. Its conditional actual acceptance probability on every reached attempt is at least $p=1/\beta-a_+>0$. Its conditional unnormalized loss is at most $\Qm_{m_+(M)}(\beta)/\beta+e_+$. Iterating the conditional acceptance bound gives probability at most $(1-p)^j$ of reaching attempt $j+1$. This argument needs only \eqref{eq:upper-row-mass}--\eqref{eq:upper-row-loss}, not a reference-model membership assumption. The packing construction in Lemma~\ref{lem:packing} uses $B+D_0m$ labels for state stopping and $\max\{B,D_0m\}$ for event stopping. A checkpoint counts only the latter output width. The first-attempt rule has acceptance one and needs no denominator. Uniform defects in \eqref{eq:defect-occupation} give \eqref{eq:uniform-reference-lower} directly. This proves every assertion.

+Suppose Proposition~\ref{prop:geometry} holds for the actually prepared comparison law, with fixed constants, and put
+$F(b,m)=\max\{b^{-2/\alpha},(bm)^{-2/(d+\alpha)}\}$.

+\begin{proof}
+Let $t_0=1-a_0$. The lower geometry bound gives
+\[t_N\Qm_{m_-}(b_-/t_N)\ge c\min\{t_0^{1+2/\alpha},t_0^{1+2/(d+\alpha)}\}F(b_-,m_-).\]

+\section{State-dependent approximate balance}
+\label{sec:approx}
+Exact task balance can be replaced by a uniform conditional certificate. The reference and the all-strategy effort inequality are left unchanged. The upper program may now have arbitrary history-dependent physical states. Write $\nu_{\theta,h}$ for the virtual report law of an attempt begun at a surviving history $h$, and suppose
+\begin{align}
+ \|\nu_{\theta,h}-\nu\|_{\TV}&\le a<1,\label{eq:approx-mass}\\
+ \left|\E_\theta[q(X)\|Z-T_Jr(X)\|^2\mid h]
+       -\int q(x)d_{r(x)}(x)\nu(dx)\right|&\le e.\label{eq:approx-task}
+\end{align}
+Here total variation between probabilities is $\sup_D|\mu(D)-\nu(D)|$. The second bound is required for every Borel $q:X\to[0,1]$ and every finite-image Borel $r:X\to H$, uniformly in $\theta,h$. It compares the complete task measure, not just report marginals or unweighted conditional variances. The program has $B$ live roles, export multiplicity $D_0$, and conditional expected attempt cost at most $\kappa_+$. The constants are certified before selecting a dictionary.
+
+\begin{theorem}[Approximate acquired-geometry transfer]\label{thm:approx}
+Under the preceding conditions, for $\beta\ge1$ with $\beta a<1$, one common program uses at most $B$ live and $D_0m$ terminal roles and satisfies
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:approx-basic}
+ \sup_\theta\E_\theta C_\tau\le\frac{\kappa_+\beta}{1-\beta a},
+ \qquad
+ \sup_\theta\E_\theta\|Z-\widehat r\|^2
+ \le\frac{\Qm_m(\beta)+\beta e}{1-\beta a}.
+\end{equation}
+It commits almost surely. Thus the alphabet counts are $B+D_0m$ for state stopping and $\max\{B,D_0m\}$ for event stopping. For a specified $b=N/\kappa_+\ge(1-a)^{-1}$, put $\beta=b/(1+ba)$. At the same physical budget $N$, the upper becomes
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:approx-budget}
+ (1+ba)\Qm_m\left(\frac b{1+ba}\right)+be.
+\end{equation}
+For $1\le b<(1-a)^{-1}$ the first-attempt rule instead has cost at most $\kappa_+$ and risk at most $\Qm_m(1)+e$. All converses in Theorem~\ref{thm:main} continue to hold at $b_-=N/\kappa_-$. No independence, renewal, or normalized-filter contraction is assumed.
+\end{theorem}
+\begin{proof}
+Take an attained $(C,h_*)$ at cap $\beta$, and accept with $q=h_*/\beta$. Its reference acceptance mass is $1/\beta$. By \eqref{eq:approx-mass}, its conditional physical acceptance probability on every surviving history is at least $p_-=1/\beta-a>0$. Consequently the probability of reaching attempt $j+1$ is at most $(1-p_-)^j$, by iterated conditioning. In particular commitment is almost sure and the expected number of attempts is at most $p_-^{-1}$. This proof does not condition on successful attempts.
+
+The nearest-center rule is finite-image and measurable. By \eqref{eq:approx-task}, the expected loss contributed by any reached attempt is at most $\Qm_m(\beta)/\beta+e$. Sum the nonnegative terminal contributions over the disjoint commitment events, and sum conditional attempt costs over the surviving attempts. Both sums are bounded by their one-attempt upper times $p_-^{-1}$, proving \eqref{eq:approx-basic}. Lemma~\ref{lem:packing} supplies the alphabet counts. The substitution for $\beta$ has $1-\beta a=(1+ba)^{-1}$ and gives the displayed budget and risk exactly. The restriction on $b$ is precisely $\beta\ge1$. With $q=1$, the first attempt always commits, regardless of the report perturbation; hence the small-budget assertion follows without dividing by an approximate acceptance mass. The converse proof uses only the admitted reference and was not altered.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}[A stable geometric regime]\label{cor:approx-geometry}
+Suppose the marked geometry of Proposition~\ref{prop:geometry} holds, the effort constants have a fixed positive ratio, and the relevant role widths differ by at most a fixed export factor. If $ba$ is bounded, $b$ is above the feasibility threshold in Theorem~\ref{thm:approx}, and
+\[
+ be\le C_0\max\{b^{-2/\alpha},(bm)^{-2/(d+\alpha)}\},
+\]
+then upper and lower risks are comparable to the same marked-geometry profile at $b,m$. These are sufficient stability conditions, not necessary error floors for every experiment.
+\end{corollary}
+\begin{proof}
+The cap $b/(1+ba)$ differs from $b$ by a bounded factor. Apply the two power terms of Proposition~\ref{prop:geometry} to \eqref{eq:approx-budget} and use the unchanged converse and fixed width factors.
+\end{proof}

+\begin{proposition}[Primitive moment certificates]\label{prop:approx-moments}
+For identity exports, let $\mu_0,\mu_1,\mu_2$ be the conditional report, vector first-moment and scalar squared-norm measures of an attempt. Suppose, uniformly over all models and surviving histories,
+\[
+ |\mu_0-\nu|(X)\le d_0,\quad
+ |\mu_1-f\nu|(X)\le d_1,\quad
+ |\mu_2-(w+\|f\|^2)\nu|(X)\le d_2,
+\]
+where $|\cdot|$ denotes total variation of scalar or finite-dimensional vector measures. If $\sup_{r\in H}\|r\|\le R_0$, then \eqref{eq:approx-mass}--\eqref{eq:approx-task} hold with
+\[
+ a\le d_0/2,\qquad e\le d_2+2R_0d_1+R_0^2d_0.
+\]
+In particular, a conditional total-variation bound $a$ on the joint report--audit law gives $e=La$ whenever all squared losses are bounded by $L$.
+\end{proposition}
+\begin{proof}
+The two report measures are probabilities, so their probability total variation is half the variation norm of their difference. Expand the loss as $\|Z\|^2-2\langle r(X),Z\rangle+\|r(X)\|^2$ and integrate the three bounded coefficient functions against the indicated signed measures. This proves the first assertion for every $q,r$ simultaneously. The last assertion applies the defining probability total-variation bound to a measurable function taking values in $[0,L]$. Vector coordinates may be taken in the affine hull of $H$; no ambient redundant coordinates are needed.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{proposition}[Sharp rare-selection scales]\label{prop:sharp-approx}
+The factor $b$ multiplying the one-attempt task defect in \eqref{eq:approx-budget} cannot be replaced by a universal smaller-order factor, even with equal report laws and one live role. Likewise the waiting denominator $1-\beta a$ in \eqref{eq:approx-basic} is attained by a zero-loss selection problem. Absence of first-moment balance can prevent every common causal program, not merely a proposed finite mixture, from attaining the reference profile.
+\end{proposition}
+\begin{proof}
+For the first assertion take $H=[-1,1]$, and let every productive call cost one and draw an independent mark uniformly on $[0,1]$. Let $D$ have mass $1/b$. In the reference model the audit is zero on $D$ and is a fresh fair sign off $D$. In a second model it is a fresh fair sign multiplied by $\sqrt{be}$ on $D$ and an ordinary fair sign off $D$, where $0\le be\le1$. Audit coins are unobserved before commitment. Both first moments vanish, all reports agree, and for every acceptance rule and response the difference of unnormalized losses is
+\[
+ be\int_D q(x)\nu(dx)\le e.
+\]
+The reference profile is zero, attained by selecting $D$ and predicting zero. In the second model every conditional residual variance is at least $be$, so every almost-surely committing program has risk at least $be$, regardless of its memory. Every zero-risk rule must commit in $D$, and the reference-count argument at the perturbed independent law forces expected calls at least $(1/\beta-a)^{-1}$. First entry into $D$ attains this value. The case $\beta=1$ can be treated with two report atoms, the second initially null. This establishes sharp waiting amplification, not a universal positive risk penalty for mere report error.

+Finally consider three models with exactly the same constant pre-audit reports and no task-changing commands. Their audits are respectively $0,+1,-1$. Their average loss is $1+\E R^2\ge1$. The constant output zero attains worst risk one. This is a complete indistinguishability proof for all legal history-dependent programs.
